base_protocol.arrival_model: independent Poisson arrivals per second; common tape across budgets
base_protocol.dispatch: global synchronous frames; released jobs only; FIFO within class
base_protocol.score: queue weighted actual frame departures divided by actual frame duration
base_protocol.budget_unit: candidate construction or feasibility attempt; seeds included
base_protocol.stopping_rule: stop arrivals at horizon, then drain the same finite prefix

protocol.role: development only; previously used confirmation seeds are excluded
protocol.eligibility: S(a) >= max(S_seed, 0.99*S_inc), using only the original paid pool
protocol.objective: J=A+terminal_weight*E[V(Q_next)] in job-seconds; main weight 1, area-only control weight 0
protocol.terminal_reference_source: one fixed feasible boundary time allocation computed from the first registered load; identical mu at every load
protocol.arrival_rate_input: registered per-class lambda, fixed through arrival window and drain
protocol.terminal_interpretation: fluid clearing at fixed mu with no arrivals beyond the next boundary; analytic surrogate rather than a second executed frame
protocol.accounting: unchanged paid candidate construction; completion reads, mean-queue and terminal second-moment evaluations counted separately for both weights
protocol.reference: v4 at K120, never K120 of a cost selector
protocol.stopping_rule: one fixed 144-run development roster; no coefficient fitting or post-result budget/seed selection

excluded_actions.reason: resident class has no arrivals in the three-class q01 protocol

certificates.arrival_model: independent Poisson job arrivals in physical time
certificates.drift_bound: E[Delta V | Q] <= B + tau_max*C - tau_min*effective_slack*sum(Q)
certificates.capacity_basis: lanes times convex hull of all admitted lane requirements/max(1,duration)

limitations: The terminal value is a fluid clearing proxy, not an exact value of future synchronous batches or a long-run flow guarantee.
The stationary arrival model remains fixed through drain, and terminal clearing assumes no further arrivals after the next boundary.
Both area-only and lookahead controls compute terminal diagnostics, so their recorded computational work includes these evaluations.
Support constraints preserve the existing drift guarantee; they do not certify the accuracy of the terminal model.
Only the paid candidate pool is optimized. This reused development roster provides no new independent confirmation.
